title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Facility-Initiated Discharge Notice Figures
content:
**Administrator's regulatory figures — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** These settings are the same in all six accommodation tiers.

| Setting | All six tiers |
|---|---|
| Written notice before a facility-initiated discharge | 30 calendar days (42 CFR 483.15(c)(4)) |
| Notice reasons that allow notice as soon as practicable | Safety of individuals endangered; health of individuals endangered; health improved; urgent medical needs; resided in the center under 30 days |
| Residence shorter than this many days allows notice as soon as practicable | 30 |
| Days a charge must be past due before a nonpayment discharge notice may issue | 60 |
| A submitted Medicaid application means the resident is not in nonpayment status for discharge purposes | Yes |
| A facility-initiated discharge waits while a timely state appeal is pending | Yes |
| A copy of every facility-initiated discharge notice goes to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman | Yes |

**Points of judgement.** A resident who has lived in the center for 29 days falls under the short-residence setting; one who has lived there 30 days does not. A room-and-board charge 59 days past due does not yet support a nonpayment notice; at 60 days it does, other conditions permitting.
